brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.requirement: Three-storey tower (bases stacked on three levels)
requirements.evidence: Level 0 has full base (0,0), half-n (0,1), half-s (0,-1), full (-1,1); level 1 has full base (0,0,1); level 2 has full base (0,0,2). Stacked via snap parts; check_build shows meshClash clear and no error issues.
Two drawers on level 0: drawer 0#0,1#cut on half-n base (0,1) and drawer 0#0,-1#cut on half-s base (0,-1). Each is locked with joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey (no lids or covers over them)
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2 hex-bin-full-div3 (3-compartment open tray) sits in the top-storey base (0,0,2) with no cover placed over it. Note: the top base has only one bin cell; the bin is an open tray with three compartments.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey hex tower. Bottom storey has two drawers on the cut faces of two half bases, held by joint bolts; the middle storey is a single full base; the top storey carries an open three-compartment bin tray. Mesh check is clear. Covers and caps were not added, so the bottom and middle storeys have open faces that the configurator reports only as info. Materials and strength are not assessed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
